:::{#cor-var-sum-indpt}
#### Variance of a sum of independent random variables

If $X$ and $Y$ are [independent](independence.qmd#def-indpt),
each [discrete](random-variables.qmd#def-discrete-rv) or [continuous](random-variables.qmd#def-continuous-rv),
with $\E{X^2} < \infty$ and $\E{Y^2} < \infty$, then:

$$\Var{X + Y} = \Var{X} + \Var{Y}$$

:::

::: proof

By @thm-indpt-uncorrelated, $\Cov{X,Y} = 0$.
Applying @cor-var-lincom2 with

$$
\begin{aligned}
a &= b \\
&= 1:
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\ba
\Var{X + Y}
&= 1^2 \Var{X} + 1^2 \Var{Y} + 2(1 \cd 1) \Cov{X,Y}
&& \text{(variance of a sum of two random variables)} \\
&= \Var{X} + \Var{Y} + 2 \Cov{X,Y}
&& \text{(simplify)} \\
&= \Var{X} + \Var{Y}
&& \text{(} \Cov{X,Y} = 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::

::: {.remark .notes}

@cor-var-lincom2 is why two variables' [covariance](#def-cov) matters for combining them:
the covariance [term](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-term) is what separates the [variance](#def-variance) of their [sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-summation)
from the sum of their variances,
and @cor-var-sum-indpt is the case where that term is 0.

:::
